external_entities.name: customer user
external_entities.description: A person at a customer company who uses the billing app as an admin or viewer.
external_entities.source_excerpt: People at a customer company use the billing app in their browser over HTTPS.
external_entities.notes: Each user belongs to one company and is either an admin or a viewer. They sign in with an email address and a password and get a session cookie.

external_entities.name: payer
external_entities.description: The recipient of an invoice email who can view the payment page.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Each invoice email sends the payer a link that ends in the invoice number.
external_entities.notes: The payer is not described as belonging to a particular customer company.

external_entities.name: support agent
external_entities.description: A support employee who uses the admin console and can open sessions as customer users.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our support agents work from the support office network.
external_entities.notes: Each agent signs in to the admin console with their own account and a one-time code.

processes.name: billing app
processes.description: The shared invoicing application used by customer users and support agents; it manages invoices, customer data, payout bank details, render jobs, payment pages and PDFs.
processes.source_excerpt: all companies share one billing app
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down whether it checks invoice company ownership or rechecks user roles when requests arrive.

processes.name: PDF renderer
processes.description: A renderer that consumes render jobs, reads invoices and writes PDFs.
processes.source_excerpt: The PDF renderer takes jobs off the queue one at a time
processes.notes: It trusts the company ID carried by each job.

processes.name: admin console
processes.description: A console used by support agents to sign in and open billing-app sessions as customer users.
processes.source_excerpt: From the admin console an agent can open a session in the billing app as any customer user.
processes.notes: The console is reachable only from the support office network; the text does not state where it runs.

data_stores.name: tenant database
data_stores.description: A shared PostgreSQL database containing every company's invoices, customers and payout bank details.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The billing app keeps every company's invoices, customers and payout bank details in one PostgreSQL database, the tenant database.
data_stores.notes: Every table has a company ID column. The database has no row-level security, and the app connects with one database account for all companies.

data_stores.name: render queue
data_stores.description: A queue carrying PDF render jobs with a company ID and invoice number.
data_stores.source_excerpt: To make a PDF, the billing app puts a render job on the render queue.
data_stores.notes: The job carries a company ID and an invoice number.

data_stores.name: PDF bucket
data_stores.description: A shared cloud bucket holding rendered PDFs under a company ID and invoice number.
data_stores.source_excerpt: writes the PDF to the PDF bucket under the company ID and the invoice number
data_stores.notes: The billing app fetches PDFs with one service credential for all companies.

data_flows.name: use billing app
data_flows.description: Customer users access the billing app from their browsers.
data_flows.source_excerpt: People at a customer company use the billing app in their browser over HTTPS.
data_flows.authentication: email address and password; session cookie

data_flows.name: open invoice
data_flows.description: A customer user opens an invoice in the billing app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a user opens an invoice, the billing app loads it by its invoice number.
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the app checks that the invoice belongs to the user's company.

data_flows.name: view payment page
data_flows.description: A payer follows an invoice link to view the payment page.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The payment page shows the invoice, the company's name and its bank details
data_flows.notes: It asks the payer to sign in to nothing.
data_flows.data_description: invoice, company name and bank details

data_flows.name: send invoice email
data_flows.description: The billing app sends an invoice email containing a link ending in the invoice number.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Each invoice email sends the payer a link that ends in the invoice number.
data_flows.data_description: invoice link ending in invoice number

data_flows.name: request PDF
data_flows.description: A user requests a PDF for an invoice.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Any user can ask for a PDF of any invoice, as often as they like.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state how the request is authenticated.

data_flows.name: enqueue render job
data_flows.description: The billing app places a PDF render job on the render queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the billing app puts a render job on the render queue
data_flows.notes: The job carries a company ID and an invoice number.

data_flows.name: take render job
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer takes render jobs from the queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The PDF renderer takes jobs off the queue one at a time

data_flows.name: read invoice
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer reads the invoice identified by the render job.
data_flows.source_excerpt: reads the invoice from the tenant database
data_flows.notes: The renderer trusts the company ID the job carries.
data_flows.data_description: invoice identified by company ID and invoice number

data_flows.name: write PDF
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer writes a rendered PDF to the bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the PDF to the PDF bucket under the company ID and the invoice number
data_flows.data_description: rendered PDF under company ID and invoice number

data_flows.name: fetch PDF
data_flows.description: The billing app fetches PDFs from the bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The billing app fetches PDFs from the bucket with one service credential for all companies.
data_flows.notes: One service credential is used for all companies.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A support agent signs in to the admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: each agent signs in to it with their own account and a one-time code

data_flows.name: open session
data_flows.description: The admin console opens a billing-app session as a customer user.
data_flows.source_excerpt: From the admin console an agent can open a session in the billing app as any customer user.
data_flows.notes: Everything the agent then does is recorded against the customer user and not against the agent.

data_flows.name: read and write tenant records
data_flows.description: The billing app queries and updates the shared tenant database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The billing app adds the company filter to each query itself
data_flows.notes: The app uses one database account for all companies and saves every invoice-edit field it receives, including the paid flag and payout bank account.
data_flows.authentication: one database account for all companies
data_flows.data_description: invoices, customers, payout bank details and user-attributed actions

trust_boundaries.name: customer company
trust_boundaries.description: The customer-company tenant zone containing people at a customer company.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Each customer company is one tenant
trust_boundaries.notes: The text describes one tenant per customer company; the shared application and stores are not placed in this zone.

trust_boundaries.name: cloud platform
trust_boundaries.description: The cloud platform in which the shared billing application and data components are described as running.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: all companies share one billing app, one database and one PDF bucket in our cloud platform

trust_boundaries.name: support office network
trust_boundaries.description: The network from which support agents work and from which the admin console is reachable.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our support agents work from the support office network.
trust_boundaries.notes: The text says the admin console is reachable only from this network but does not state that the console runs there.
